h: What a Pier Session Looks Like
p: Pier fishing is about as accessible as sea angling gets. There's no need to clamber over rocks or wade into surf, you're standing on solid boards with the water already deep enough beneath you, and you can pack up and grab a hot drink whenever you fancy. For a newcomer, that makes it a far gentler introduction than a day on a charter boat.

Along this stretch of the Essex coast, anglers commonly target flatfish, whiting and codling in the colder months, with bass and smoothhounds drawing people out in the warmer weather. What turns up on any given day depends on the tide, the season and a good dollop of luck, which is half the appeal. A local tackle shop is the best place to ask what's showing and which baits are working, and they'll usually sort you out with ragworm, lugworm or squid.

Be mindful of other people on the pier, especially when casting, and always look behind you before you swing a rod. Keep your gear tidy so nobody trips over it, and take all your line and rubbish home with you, as discarded fishing line is a real danger to seabirds. If you catch something undersized, return it quickly and gently. Check any size limits and pier rules before your first cast.

Once the rods are packed away, Clacton's seafront has plenty of chippies and cafés to warm up in. Further along the coast, Walton-on-the-Naze has its own long pier and a backwater famous for its wildlife, while the Naze cliffs are a fascinating spot for a blustery walk.
